title: Never paste private info into a chatbot
intro: Chatbots help with homework, ideas and explanations. But what you type or paste into them can be saved and read later.
So never put passwords, your address, phone number, photos of documents or other people's secrets into a chatbot.
A simple rule: if you wouldn't write it on the board at school, don't write it in a chatbot.

game.prompt: What's OK to type into a chatbot, and what never is?

items.text: A question about fractions from your homework
items.explain: A learning question with no personal details is exactly what chatbots are good for.

items.text: Your password, to check if it's strong
items.explain: A password only goes where it belongs. You can ask about the rules without typing it.

items.text: A made-up story you wrote about a dragon, to get ideas
items.explain: A made-up story with no real details is fine to share.

items.text: A photo of your parents' passport or ID card
items.explain: Personal documents are some of the most sensitive information there is. Never paste them into a chatbot.

items.text: A list of spelling words to practise
items.explain: Practice words aren't personal information. Good luck!

items.text: A secret a friend told you
items.explain: Other people's secrets aren't ours to share, not even with a chatbot.

quiz.question: What can happen to what you type into a chatbot?
options: It can be saved and read later
It vanishes forever once you send it
quiz.explain: Messages can be saved, so private information stays out of chatbots.

quiz.question: You want to know if your password is strong. What do you do?
options: Ask what makes a password strong, without typing it
Send it to a friend to check
quiz.explain: You can learn what makes a password strong without showing it to anyone.

quiz.question: You need help with a form that has personal details on it. What do you do?
options: Take a photo and paste it into a chatbot
quiz.explain: Forms with personal details get filled in with a parent, not a chatbot.

summary: A chatbot is a good tool for questions and ideas, but what you type can be saved. Never type passwords, addresses, documents or other people's secrets into one.
